properties.chose: Option (a), as built in P4b, Anthony 2026-10-19 ("go with your recommendations"): a far premise reads the far node's truth live on every call; stale = the far node is gone, unreachable = the far design could not be read, both unknown; a far design that merely moved since the link keeps its live truth and upstream_status still flags it. (b) was not taken because a busy proof design would blank every citation of it until re-linked, and it cannot judge an unpinned link at all (the measured calc case). Also settled with it: walks cross designs only through a hub's address; a bare-id delete of an id nothing holds returns {deleted:false}; prefixes outside ID_PREFIXES are refused on a bare id. Far readings are uncached for now.
properties.decision: Built in P4b as (a), for the owner to confirm or turn: (a) LIVE: the far node's truth and proof status are read fresh on every call, so they are current by construction; stale = the far node is gone (unknown), unreachable = the far design could not be read on this call (unknown); a far design that changed since the link was made is still reported by upstream_status (link_far_end_moved, which needs a pin) and does not change the premise's truth. (b) ACKNOWLEDGED: a far end whose design moved since the link (fingerprint_at_link differs from now) reads unknown "stale" until re-linked, as upstream_status already asks — so a busy proof design makes every citation of it unknown until someone re-links. (c) BOTH: live truth, plus a `moved_since_link` flag beside it on the reading.
properties.name: SETTLED 2026-10-19 — option (a): a premise in another design reads the far node's truth as computed now; "stale" means the far node is gone, and a far design that merely moved still reads its live truth
properties.rationale: req:reasoning-crosses-designs-within-a-hub part 3 says stale or unreachable far ends read as such, never as holding, and part 1 says the premise carries the far node's computed truth. (a) reads part 1 as a live computation, so what a re-link would acknowledge is already what is read; it also works when calc does not pin the proof design (the measured case: no fingerprint_at_link, so (b) could not judge staleness at all). Counter-argument: (b) keeps dec:ask-not-repair's discipline that a person re-reads a moved far end before relying on it again; under (a) a far theorem whose wording changed but whose proof still holds is relied on silently. (c) is cheap only if the far content hash is computed per call, which (a) avoids. Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019Xbw6PG9mXJiU2Sb421fnq
